R3B-bear-backcountry-0002.name: By Lynx Creek
R3B-bear-backcountry-0002.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R3B-bear-backcountry-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burn from 2017 (fire C31489), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 15 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Lynx Creek 80 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Blue River, about 129 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.56927, -120.55296, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 7.3 km N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 973 m, about 243 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 220 m E of the spot at 1,224 m (52.63513, -120.53856). Water: Lynx Creek 60 m W (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-15, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R3B-bear-backcountry-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 5-15: about 859 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.09 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
